images.title: Check with factor pairs
images.purpose: Recap how to check a factor list is complete: each factor pairs with a partner, using 18 as a small example.
images.composition: The six factors of 18 sit in one ordered row in the centre, joined by three nested arcs above them, with the prime factorisation as a small line above and a count line below.
exact_structure: Small line at the top centre: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3.
One row of exactly 6 rounded number chips in order: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.
Exactly 3 nested arcs above the row: an outer teal #0072B2 arc joining 1 and 18, a middle amber #E69F00 arc joining 2 and 9, an inner reddish purple #CC79A7 arc joining 3 and 6.
Below the row, in green #009E73, the line 6 factors, no repeats.
rejection: an arc joining two chips whose product is not 18
more or fewer than 6 chips, or chips out of order
any of the numbers 90, 105, 132, 360 or 840 appearing
images.takeaway: Pair each factor with its partner; if every pair multiplies to the number and none is missing, the list is complete.
images.description: The factors 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18 in a row with three arcs pairing 1 with 18, 2 with 9 and 3 with 6.
images.context: Shown beside the practice tool for building all the factors of a number.
images.teaching_notes: Use the arcs to check each list: every factor should have exactly one partner.

image_decisions.why: Factor pair arcs give a quick visual check that a factor list is complete.
